title: Morphisms between alteration objects are maximally finite dominant and finite type
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning a scheme admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $\ell$ be a prime. Let $X\to S$ and $T\to S$ be objects of $\operatorname{alt}/S$ [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. Thus both sources are reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme], both structural maps are of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and each generic point of either source maps to a generic point of $S$ with finite residue-field extension [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-weil-residue-field, def-pc-field-extension]. Here a generic point of a component means a point whose closure is that component. For every $S$-morphism $u:X\to T$, the morphism $u$ is of finite type and sends each generic point $x$ of a component of $X$ to a generic point of a component of $T$, with $\kappa(x)/\kappa(u(x))$ finite through the induced residue-field map. These assertions include the empty source.

source.place: Expose II Proposition 1.1.10 and 1.2.3, printed pp.24--25, for maximal dominance and finite generic residue extensions. Finite type is the affine finite-generation cancellation and Noetherian quasi-compactness used in the proof of 1.2.6, printed p.25.

proof.text: Write $a:X\to S$ and $b:T\to S$ for the structure maps, so $b\circ u=a$. By the object definition [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology], $a,b$ are of finite type. Hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X,T$ Noetherian; in particular $X$ is quasi-compact and $T$ locally Noetherian. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated], $T$ is quasi-separated. Clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] now makes $u$ quasi-compact. Clause (a) of [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target], applied to $b\circ u=a$, makes $u$ locally of finite type. These two properties are exactly finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. No separatedness of $b$ is required.

source.place: Tags 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian) and 01T8 (lemma-permanence-finite-type); properties.tex Tag 01OY (lemma-locally-Noetherian-quasi-separated); schemes.tex Tag 03GI (lemma-quasi-compact-permanence). This supplies the finite-type input implicit in ILO II 1.2.6.

proof.text: Fix a generic point $x$ of a component of $X$, and put $s=a(x)$ and $y=u(x)$. The alteration-object hypothesis makes $s$ generic in a component of $S$ [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. By [lem-sc-irreducible-components-cover], $y$ lies in a component $C$ of $T$, and [lem-sc-scheme-sober] gives its generic point $y\prime$, so $y\in\overline{\{y\prime\}}$. Again the object hypothesis makes $s\prime=b(y\prime)$ generic in a component of $S$. Continuity of $b$ gives $s\in\overline{\{s\prime\}}$, whence $\overline{\{s\}}\subseteq\overline{\{s\prime\}}$. Both are irreducible components; maximality [def-weil-irreducible-components] forces equality, and uniqueness of their generic point [lem-sc-scheme-sober] gives $s=s\prime$. Thus $y,y\prime$ both lie over $s$.

source.place: Expose II Proposition 1.1.10, proof, printed p.24: choose a maximal generalization of y and compare its image with s; component existence and sobriety are Stacks Tags 004W and 01IS.

proof.text: For the component generic point $y\prime$ of $T$, the object hypothesis gives $\kappa(y\prime)/\kappa(s)$ finite [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. Apply [lem-trf-finite-residue-point-closed-in-fibre] to the finite-type map $b:T\to S$ at $y\prime$: this point is closed in $T_s$. The first projection identifies the topology of $T_s$ with the subspace $b^{-1}(s)$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Since $y,y\prime$ lie in that subspace and $y\in\overline{\{y\prime\}}$ in $T$, the subspace-closure identity puts $y$ in the closure of $y\prime$ in $T_s$. Closedness gives $y=y\prime$. Thus $u(x)$ is a component generic point of $T$.

source.place: Expose II Proposition 1.1.10, proof, printed p.24: equality y=y prime in the fibre; Stacks Tag 01TE (morphisms.tex, lemma-algebraic-residue-field-extension-closed-point-fibre) and Tag 01K1 (schemes.tex, lemma-fibre-topological).

proof.text: The induced maps on residue fields [def-weil-residue-field] give $\kappa(s)\to\kappa(y)\to\kappa(x)$. Their composite is the map for $a=b\circ u$: on local rings this is composition, and passing to quotients by the maximal ideals preserves composition. Each map is injective because it is a field homomorphism [def-pc-field-extension], so these are compatible subfields. The object hypothesis gives $\kappa(x)$ finite-dimensional over $\kappa(s)$ [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. Choose a finite $\kappa(s)$-spanning family in $\kappa(x)$. The same family spans over the larger subfield $\kappa(y)$, because every expression with coefficients in $\kappa(s)$ is an expression with coefficients in $\kappa(y)$. Hence $\kappa(x)/\kappa(y)$ is finite through the specified induced map. This holds for every component generic point $x$. If $X$ is empty there are no such points; Step 1 still proves finite type. If $S$ or $T$ is empty, the existence of the structural maps or of $u$ forces the appropriate source to be empty.
